A1.justification: Both complete 19-page PDFs describe SelfHVD. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched despite the revised title and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original deblurring experiments on GoProShake, HVD, BSD, RealBlur and RBVD, together with component ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds cross-device deblurring results, temporal-consistency measurements and computational-efficiency results.

M1.justification: Sharp-frame selection, SEA-RAFT masking, SEVD with RSCR/SIS, SCSCM and the training objectives remain unchanged. ESTRNN already appears in v1's test-time experiments; its expanded evaluation does not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: HVD deblurring evaluation expands from Huawei P40 to Xiaomi 15 and iPhone 16, with Huawei-trained models tested on the additional devices. v1 examined these brands only for sharp-frame presence. RealBlur pretraining is removed from Appendix D.5/Table F, although RealBlur evaluation remains.

E2.justification: v2 adds Blur2Blur to the BSD/RealBlur/RBVD comparison and fully supervised ESTRNN to GoProShake. HVD comparisons newly include fully supervised IFIRNN, ESTRNN and RVRT; BasicVSR++ was already evaluated in v1's appendix. These additions broaden the comparison sets across the principal experiments.

E3.justification: v2 adds temporal evaluation using tOF, tLP, FVD and VBench, plus parameter-count, FLOP and inference-time measurements. HVD testing expands from 20 to 60 videos, and the main benchmark configurations include ESTRNN. Existing augmentation, optimizer and learning-rate settings remain unchanged; Appendix E.1 clarifies data usage without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses examine cross-device generalization, temporal consistency and computational cost across backbones. The RealBlur-pretraining ablation condition and the low-light noise failure case are removed. Existing mask, SEVD/SCSCM, optical-flow and selection-interval analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify random seed 0 and report point estimates. Neither reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds device, comparator, backbone, efficiency and temporal-result entries and removes RealBlur-pretraining results. GoProShake SelfHVD-IFIRNN PSNR changes from 34.23 to 34.32; DaDeblur's RBVD PSNR changes from 27.08 to 27.02. HVD scores are extensively revised: SelfHVD-BasicVSR++ changes from 31.6400/0.4338 in v1 Table 2 to 28.0040/0.2175 on HVD-Huawei in v2 Table 1. The PDFs do not explain these HVD revisions, so they do not establish a method-level performance change.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and dataset-synthesis derivation are retained. Appendix Equations A–G become Equations 15–21 without substantive mathematical changes; no new theorem, proof or formal assumption appears.

C1.justification: The title and abstract broaden the stated target from mobile phones to handheld shooting devices. The central contributions and claims concerning sharp-clue supervision, SEVD/SCSCM and superiority to existing self-supervised methods remain.

C2.justification: v2 removes Appendix F's explanation that nighttime noise degrades restoration and remains visible, together with the proposed future remedy. Appendix E.4 newly interprets lower tOF/tLP as evidence of better temporal consistency. Existing mechanism explanations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 explicitly documents supervised and self-supervised training/evaluation data usage. Table G adds parameter counts, FLOPs and inference times, and Table 1 identifies the comparison methods' ESTRNN backbone. The reported access link changes from a GitHub repository to a project page.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chu et al. (2020) for temporal metrics and removes the cited textual-degradation restoration and exposure-bracketing papers. The central positioning against synthetic-blur self-supervision remains unchanged. Reference renumbering and publication metadata updates do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 revises device terminology and Related Work prose, introduces numbered sections and a separate ablation section, subdivides Appendix E, adds acknowledgements and moves references before the supplement. Most method explanations and the overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: v2 consolidates GoProShake/HVD tables and qualitative comparisons, redistributes examples between the main text and appendix, expands comparison columns, and reworks Figures 3–4. It adds Tables G–H and removes the noise-failure Figure L. The display and layout revisions extend substantially beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: Cross-device HVD tests, matched ESTRNN comparisons and temporal measurements strengthen applicability and video-quality evidence beyond v1. Clearer data-use documentation also helps. These gains are limited by unexplained HVD score revisions, unreconciled RVRT values in v2 Tables 1 and B, and removal of the low-light limitation and failure example, which reduce reporting transparency.
